title: Wheatstone and Meter Bridge
notes: A Wheatstone bridge has four resistances P, Q, R and S, with a galvanometer across one diagonal and the battery across the other. At balance the galvanometer current is zero and P/Q = R/S.

The metre bridge is that bridge with a uniform 100 cm wire as two of the arms. If the jockey balances at length l1 from the left, the left wire resistance is proportional to l1 and the right to l2 = 100 − l1.

If the known resistance R is in the left gap and the unknown X is in the right gap, the balance condition is X/R = l2/l1, or the swapped form if the gaps are swapped. The diagram decides which length is which.
A uniform wire is essential, because the ratio of resistances is the ratio of lengths only when the resistance per centimetre is constant.
End corrections add a few millimetres for the copper strips. A precise unknown repeats the measurement with the gaps swapped and averages the two values of X.
Heating the wire changes its resistance per centimetre, so the current is kept small and the balance is found with a light touch of the jockey.
confusion: ❌ 'A meter bridge can measure any resistance accurately.' ✅ It is accurate only for *moderate* resistances (≈1 Ω to 1 kΩ); very high or very low resistances give poor null points.
❌ 'The null point is always at the center (50 cm) of the meter bridge.' ✅ The null point shifts depending on the ratio of resistances; it is at 50 cm *only* when the two known resistances are equal.
❌ 'Wheatstone bridge and meter bridge are completely different instruments.' ✅ A meter bridge is essentially a *Wheatstone bridge* with a uniform 1-meter wire replacing two arms.
Balance is zero galvanometer current, not zero battery current.
l1 and l2 must match the gaps in the formula.
The wire ratio is not the resistance ratio if the wire is not uniform.
100 cm is the wire, not the length of the unknown resistor.

exercises.question: A metre bridge balances at 40.0 cm from the left. The known resistance in the left gap is 2.0 Ω and the unknown is in the right gap. Find X.
steps: With R on the left and X on the right, X/R = l2/l1.
A balance at 40 cm, not 50 cm, means the right-hand resistance is larger, which matches 3.0 > 2.0.
